sentences.text: The RBI directions do not create a general prohibition for all non-individual borrowers; for loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 January 2026, cases outside paragraphs 261(1) and 261(2) may have pre-payment charges as per the UCB’s approved policy, and for term loans any charge must be based on the amount prepaid.

A 2% foreclosure charge can therefore fit the RBI framework for a corporate borrower only if the loan is in that residual category and the charge is disclosed in the sanction letter and loan agreement.
If the loan is an existing floating-rate term loan sanctioned before 31 December 2025, the directions say the UCB shall not charge pre-payment charges.
I could not confirm whether the loan falls under the permitted or prohibited category because the sanction or renewal date, and whether the loan is floating-rate, were not provided.

missing.searched: UCB pre-payment applicability under paragraphs 260 and 261 depends on whether the loan was sanctioned or renewed before or on/after the stated dates.
The evidence does not state whether the corporate borrower’s loan is floating-rate, which matters for paragraphs 260 and 261(4).
